mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 5.0 for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of two consecutive quarterly declines in GDPC1 (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which increases discount rates and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 150,000 for two consecutive months signals labor market strength, which supports consumer demand and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when PAYEMS > 150,000 for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,000 for two consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when HOUST < 1,000 for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3.0% for three consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which leads to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).
